title: Shell-first SDK quickstart runbook and smoke telemetry
content:
Context and intent:

This is a working runbook for a "shell-first" SDK onboarding flow. The goal is a one-minute developer experience that users can run from their terminal to: install the SDK client, authenticate with a short-lived test API key, run a simple generate/chat/embeddings command, and ship minimal telemetry so we can validate the happy path in the wild.

Why shell-first?
- Fastest path to the first success: copy-paste commands vs language-specific installs.
- Good for demos, interviews, and CI smoke checks.
- Lets us verify networking/region routing and basic telemetry before we invest in language-specific tutorials.

High-level requirements:
1) A single script (sh) that works on macOS/linux (and reasonable behavior on Windows via WSL).
2) Minimal dependencies: curl, jq (optional but recommended), unzip for binaries.
3) An ephemeral credential flow: issue test-key for 1 hour from the Console or via a dedicated token endpoint.
4) SDK binary (tiny shim) that proxies requests with sensible defaults (model, region, telemetry tags).
5) Built-in smoke tests: generate, chat, embeddings.
6) Telemetry hooks that emit a single batched event after the happy path completes.
7) Clear failure messages and next step links.

Runbook steps (author/maintainer):

A) Prepare release artifacts
- Build tiny SDK binary (go/python shim) that accepts: --api-key, --region, --model, --profile.
- Publish zipped binaries to the cdn path: https://cdn.redwood.ai/sdk-shell/shell-sdk-<version>.zip
- Create a compact manifest (text) with supported models and default region.

B) Example onboarding script (concept):
1) curl -fsSL https://cdn.redwood.ai/sdk-shell/install-latest.sh | sh
   - install-latest.sh will: download zip, unpack to ~/.local/bin/redwood-shell, add minimal profile file (~/.redwood/profile) if absent.
2) export REDWOOD_TEST_KEY=eyJr... (or prompt for paste)
3) redwood-shell generate --prompt "Write a 3-line haiku about reliability" --json | jq .
4) redwood-shell chat --system "You are a concise assistant." --message "Summarize this repo in two bullets."
5) redwood-shell embed --text "What is Redwood Inference?" --output result.json

C) Smoke telemetry design (one batched payload)
- Event name: sdk.shell.quickstart.completed
- Payload fields (avoid PII): sdk_version, bin_sha256, platform, region, model, duration_ms, success_steps (list), error_code (if any), trial_tier (if set).
- Emit only after the happy path completes. If any step fails, emit sdk.shell.quickstart.failed with same fields plus step_name and human_error_message.
- Rate limiting: client should send at most 1 telemetry event per unique api_key per 24h.
- Redaction: never include full API key or user-supplied content. Only hash of api_key, and a boolean flag for whether user pasted network-restricted key.

D) Minimal smoke tests and expected outputs
- generate: expect non-empty text and tokens_consumed > 0.
- chat: expect a single assistant reply with length > 16 chars.
- embed: expect a numeric vector of length matching the model profile (e.g., 1536).
- exit code semantics: 0 = success-run (all three), 1 = partial (some assertions failed), 2 = fatal (install/auth failure).

E) Troubleshooting map (common failures)
- install fails: suggest curl -fsSL alternative, check unzip available, check PATH write perms. Provide commands: mkdir -p ~/.local/bin; curl -o /tmp/sdk.zip <url>; unzip -o /tmp/sdk.zip -d ~/.local/bin; chmod +x ~/.local/bin/redwood-shell
- auth error 401: check REDWOOD_TEST_KEY variable; run redwood-shell auth-validate --api-key $REDWOOD_TEST_KEY to get human-friendly error.
- network timeout to region: try --region us-west-2 or use --insecure-skip-tls for internal debugging (documented as temporary).
- model mismatch 422: fallback to model alias in manifest, suggest --model rwd-mini-v1.

F) Observability and experimental metrics to track
- conversion: quickstart-run-started -> quickstart-run-completed (ratio)
- time-to-first-token (ms) measured across runs
- top-3 failure steps and their ratios (install, auth, network)
- client bin versions and platform distribution (macOS, linux-x86_64, arm64)
- test-key hash churn: how many unique hashes per week (indicates trial abuse/automation)

G) Security and privacy checklist
- Do not log full API keys; store only first 8 chars + sha256(key) for lookup.
- Telemetry must natively respect DO_NOT_TRACK environment variables.
- Provide an opt-out: redwood-shell --telemetry=off or set REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0

H) Minimal copy for the quickstart terminal output (friendly UX)
- After install: "Installed redwood-shell vX.Y to ~/.local/bin. Run `redwood-shell quickstart --help` to see a one-minute demo."
- On success: green-check emoji, brief summary and link to next steps (language SDKs, embedding playground, console).
- On failure: one-sentence cause and a single actionable command to recover. E.g., "Auth failed: paste a test key (from Console > Quickkeys) and run: export REDWOOD_TEST_KEY=...; redwood-shell auth-validate"

I) Open questions / follow ups (TODOs)
- Do we want per-enterprise telemetry allow-list (for enterprise customers that opt-in to have telemetry routed to their org)?
- Can the quickstart produce a permalink to a live trace in Console (requires short-lived sample traces ingestion)?
- Should we include a one-click GitHub Actions workflow that runs the shell quickstart as a weekly canary? (good candidate)
- UX: add a compact interactive flow (arrow prompts) vs purely script-first. Which is higher conversion?

J) Release checklist for maintainers
- [ ] publish binary and manifest to CDN path
- [ ] update install script checksum and release notes
- [ ] create short demo video (1 minute) and a TL;DR text for marketing
- [ ] wire telemetry event to ingestion pipeline and add dashboard (conversion & failure heatmap)
- [ ] create GitHub Action workflow under infra/canaries to run quickstart weekly

Contact and notes:
- Primary owner: Leah Park (eng-developer-experience).
- Engineering contacts: Marco Nguyen (cli lead), Priya Kapoor (telemetry), Jonas Reed (security).

Scratchpad: sample quickstart command sequence to test locally:
1) curl -fsSL https://cdn.redwood.ai/sdk-shell/install-latest.sh | sh
2) export REDWOOD_TEST_KEY=<paste-test-key>
3) redwood-shell quickstart --run-all --telemetry=on

Keep this doc as the seed for the user-facing quickstart guide (docs.redwood.ai/quickstarts/shell-sdk). This runbook should remain internal until telemetry and canary automation are validated.

Notes for copy editing later: turn troubleshooting map into an expandable web widget; convert the telemetry schema into a single-line JSON example for the console docs.

(End of draft)
